papers.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
papers.abstract: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

papers.title: Pion and kaon electromagnetic form factors in a flavor-dressed contact interaction: the role of Nf-screening on dynamical chiral symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: We compute the electromagnetic form factors of the pion and the kaon in a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose effective coupling depends on the number of active light flavors Nf , so that dynamical chiral symmetry breaking is screened as Nf grows toward the chiral transition. The calculation uses the rainbow-ladder truncation of the Schwinger-Dyson and Bethe-Salpeter equations with proper-time regularization, and it includes the dressed quark-photon vertex obtained from its own inhomogeneous Bethe-Salpeter equation in the same truncation. At Nf = 2 the model reproduces the established contact interaction values of the meson masses, decay constants and condensates, and the charge radii rpi = 0.447 fm and rK = 0.417 fm, which undershoot experiment by about one third, as is known for this class of interactions. We therefore restrict every comparison to Q2 less then or equal to 0.6 GeV2, confront it with the NA7 data and with one-loop chiral perturbation theory, and focus on the response to Nf . Both radii grow monotonically with Nf , and the growth survives every variation of the screening function and of the infrared confinement scale that we test. The growth is carried by the quark core rather than by the vector-meson dressing: between Nf = 2 and 6 the bare-vertex contribution to <r2pi> rises from 0.097 to 0.226 fm2, while the dressing contribution moves from 0.102 to 0.127 fm2 even though the rho pole drops from 0.93 to 0.70 GeV. The finite strange mass slows the kaon response only moderately.

papers.title: Evidence for quark+quark pairing in proton formation
papers.abstract: The question of pairing between quarks inside baryons is addressed by calculating the fragmentation functions that describe production of nucleons (protons and neutrons) in high-energy collisions and comparing attendant predictions with phenomenological global fits to available data and directly with data on hadron multiplicities. The fragmentation functions are obtained from nucleon parton distribution functions using the Drell-Levy-Yan relation and subsequently solving a coupled set of pion, kaon, and nucleon jet cascade equations. Strong empirical evidence is found for the presence of diquark correlations. In comparison with global fits, $d$ (down) quark to proton fragmentation ($d\to p$) exhibits the clearest signals. The strongest evidence is found in comparisons with the momentum-dependent proton multiplicity distribution: FFs built from a proton wave function that contains diquark correlations deliver a $z$-profile that is fully consistent with available data, whereas that obtained from a no-pairing wave function is disfavoured by data at the $9\sigma$ level.

papers.title: NuSTEC Review: Current Experimental and Theoretical Challenges of Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
papers.abstract: The precise measurement of neutrino properties is among the highest priorities in fundamental particle physics, involving many experimental and theoretical efforts worldwide. Since the experiments rely on the interactions of neutrinos in the nuclear environment, the planned advances in the scope and precision of these experiments require a commensurate effort in understanding and modeling the hadronic and nuclear physics of these interactions, as incorporated in neutrino event generators. This modeling is essential to every phase of the experimental analyses, and the theoretical uncertainties play an important role in interpreting experimental results. In this Review of current challenges, we summarize the open questions in neutrino-nucleus interactions at GeV-scale energies, and discuss in detail the potential impacts of these unknowns on the measurement of neutrino properties, using the determination of oscillation parameters as a central example. After an Executive Summary and a concise Overview of the issues, we address how the neutrino event generators treat these challenges, how electron-nucleus interactions can help understanding these challenges and the important unanswered questions for each underlying physics process---from quasi-elastic to deep-inelastic scattering. Across every topic, we find that current challenges can be met only through active support and collaboration among specialists in strong interactions and electroweak physics, including theorists and experimentalists from both the nuclear and high-energy physics communities.

papers.title: Flavor decomposition of the nucleon axial and tensor charges from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We determine the nucleon axial and tensor charges using four ensembles of twisted-mass clover-improved fermions with approximately equal physical volumes of about 5.5~fm and four lattice spacings, $ a=0.05$~fm, 0.06~fm, 0.07~fm, and 0.08~fm. The mass of the degenerate up and down, strange and charm quarks are tuned to approximately their physical values. We compute both connected and disconnected contributions to determine the isovector and isoscalar charges and their flavour decomposition. For the nucleon isovector axial charge we find $g_A^{u-d}=1.263(34)(26)$, in agreement with the experimental value. For the isoscalar axial charge we find $g_A^{u+d}=0.458(16)(1)$, while for the corresponding tensor charges we find $g_T^{u-d}=0.951(21)(5)$ and $g_T^{u+d}=0.556(16)(5)$.

papers.title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
papers.abstract: Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. However, its power is limited by the small forward multiplicity in light-ion collisions. In this work, we study the effect of the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections on the symmetric cumulants in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV using EPOS4 with an ATLAS-like acceptance. Using the law of total covariance, the symmetric cumulant is separated into a selected part, which follows the differences between the $q_n$ classes, and a residual part within them. It is observed that in OO collisions the correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$ remain almost entirely within the $q_2$ classes, unlike in Pb--Pb collisions. Nevertheless, events with the smallest $q_2$ in central OO collisions show weaker correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$, which is attributed to $v_4$ approaching its linear response. In Pb--Pb collisions, the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections act separately on the two factors of the nonlinear coupling of $v_5$, which establishes a way to isolate them experimentally.

papers.title: How to isolate charm production mechanisms using charm-anticharm rapidity and azimuthal angle differences
papers.abstract: Charm production in hadronic collisions proceeds via many different processes, which makes it hard to calculate from first principles. Using PYTHIA simulations, we study correlations between charm and anticharm hadrons and show that hard-process charm, final-state splitting charm, and initial-state-shower charm populate markedly different regions of rapidity and azimuthal-angle difference. In particular, selections on the pair rapidity separation, $\Delta y$, can strongly enrich or suppress the near-side final-state splitting contribution and thereby provide experimental sensitivity to the different production processes. A comparison with existing LHCb $D^0\bar{D}^0$ correlation measurements from Run 1 motivates more differential studies using the substantially larger LHC data sets now available. Extending such measurements to heavy-ion collisions could further distinguish medium modifications of charm produced directly in the hard scattering from charm originating from a parent gluon, providing a new handle on the different interactions of heavy quarks and gluons with the quark-gluon plasma.

papers.title: Short-range dynamics of $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ in a coupled-channel framework
papers.abstract: We study the short-range dynamics in the coupled-channel description of the $S$-wave $D \bar{D}^*$ and $DD^*$ systems for $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$, respectively. Contact interactions are related through scalar- and vector-meson exchange saturation, while pion exchange is included explicitly with its local term subtracted. The coupled Lippmann-Schwinger equations incorporate the self-energy of the unstable $D^*$ mesons, thereby accounting for the three-body $D \bar{D} \pi$ ($D D\pi$) dynamics. Fixing the contact interaction from the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ pole, we trace the predicted $X(3872)$ pole as the local magnetic dipole term from vector-meson exchange is varied. Retaining this term in full produces the shallowest poles, which remain approximately $5$--$12~\mathrm{MeV}$ below the observed $X(3872)$ mass. It is found that the pion exchange has a moderate effect on the binding energy and a stronger effect on the isospin violation for the $X(3872)$ state. The residual tension between the pure-molecular bound descriptions of $X(3872)$ and $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ is analyzed with the Feshbach projection. This analysis indicates a $DD^*$ interaction weaker than that implied by the purely molecular fits, and shows that the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ state instead arises from the mixing of the $DD^{*}$ channel with a compact $cc\bar{u}\bar{d}$ state. We further examine the spatial structure using Born--Oppenheimer effective field theory. For separation radii of $0.5$--$1.5~\mathrm{fm}$, the combined charmonium and short-distance tetraquark weight in $X(3872)$ is $3.0$--$9.7\%$, while the short-distance weight in $T_{cc}(3875)^+$ is $1.3$--$14.4\%$. These results favor retaining the local vector-exchange contribution within the saturation framework and motivate a joint treatment of molecular and compact dynamics for the $T_{cc}(3875)^+$.

papers.title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
papers.abstract: Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 \phi)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer R\'enyi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. The modulation is predicted to be maximally strong and independent of the transverse momentum imbalance, $q$, from a dilute (BFKL) perspective, while it is considerably suppressed by saturation effects. In diffraction, we observe that the pair is always entangled and exhibits the same properties found in diffractive DIS. We explain how these properties follow directly from the exclusive and eikonal nature of the Pomeron exchange. We trace this behavior to a spin-density matrix of rank at most two with maximally mixed marginals. For this class of states, entanglement and Bell nonlocality coincide even when the state is mixed, while the explicit form of the light-front helicity amplitudes ensures that both persist in the whole phase space. We suggest accessing the spin correlations in unpolarized hadron collisions through the Collins and dihadron fragmentation functions. We point out that, in inclusive production, for massless quarks, suitably chosen double-Collins asymmetries provide promising entanglement witnesses.

papers.title: Hadronic final-state effects on open-charm production at LHC energies
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of hadronic final-state interactions on open-charm observables in pp and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC energies within the microscopic Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD) transport approach. Calculations with and without charm-hadron rescattering are compared with ALICE measurements and predictions of the Statistical Hadronization Model for charm. The relative integrated $D$-meson multiplicities are essentially insensitive to hadronic interactions. PHSD reproduces the weak system dependence of the nonstrange $D$-meson ratios and the increase of $D_s^+/D^0$ from pp to Pb+Pb collisions, consistent with the statistical-model trend from strangeness undersaturation towards equilibrium. In contrast, hadronic rescattering redistributes the transverse momentum spectra at low and intermediate momenta and enhances the elliptic flow. These results demonstrate the importance of accounting for the hadronic evolution when extracting QGP properties from differential open-charm observables.

papers.title: HEART: a resonance-cascade model of soft hadron production in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c
papers.abstract: Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 identified-hadron spectra in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This paper supplies an event-level realization of that picture, the HEART model (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), and tests it on the published NA49 data. Single diffraction, double diffraction, and non-diffractive exchange produce color-singlet excited systems. Each system is a catalogued resonance below a duality boundary of 1.7 to 2.2 GeV or a member of a resonant continuum above it. It de-excites by successive two-body transitions with exact conservation laws, and one-pion exchange produces the leading neutrons. Fourteen parameters are fitted to 1,254 points of the $\pi^\pm$, $K^\pm$, $p$, and $\bar{p}$ double-differential cross sections and eight neutron points. Under an error model that profiles the correlated systematic uncertainties, with a declared 5% model floor, the fit yields $\chi^2 = 2263$ on 1248 degrees of freedom. On the same points, EPOS-LHC, UrQMD, and PYTHIA 8 at their published tunes give $\chi^2$ values 4.2 to 14.4 times higher. The model needs no central source. The forward $K^+$ deficit, the forward $K^*(892)^0$ excess, and the flat $\Lambda$ $x_F$ distribution point to the momentum sharing at the vertex where the leading baryon turns into a hyperon. The $\Xi^-$ reaches 0.61 of the NA61/SHINE yield. The charged multiplicity of a heavy excited system grows linearly with its mass, faster than in $e^+e^-$ annihilation. The observables that distinguish a cascade from string and fireball models lie in the fragmentation region, where wide-acceptance fixed-target spectrometers can measure them.

papers.title: From oxygen to lead: testing a common QGP description with high-$p_\perp$ probes
papers.abstract: The observation of suppression and finite high-$p_\perp$ elliptic anisotropy in O+O and Ne+Ne raises the question of whether a common quark--gluon plasma (QGP) description can simultaneously account for both observables across systems from oxygen to lead. We present predictions using event-by-event bulk evolution constrained by soft-sector observables and coupled to DREENA radiative and collisional energy loss, with the same microscopic parameter set for O+O, Ne+Ne, Xe+Xe, and Pb+Pb. The calculation reproduces the observed ordering of suppression and predicts elliptic anisotropies of comparable magnitude across the four systems in 10--20$\%$ collisions. We predict a modest centrality dependence of $v_2^{\mathrm{SP}}$ and a more pronounced decrease of $v_3^{\mathrm{SP}}$ toward peripheral light-ion collisions, in contrast to the corresponding trends in larger systems. In light ions, we predict that $v_2^{\mathrm{SP}}/(1-R_{AA})$ is nearly independent of momentum at high $p_\perp$. We further predict that the differential ratio $v_2\{4\}/v_2\{2\}$ depends only weakly on momentum at high $p_\perp$, with magnitudes and centrality trends broadly comparable to those of the measured soft-sector ratios, suggesting that the soft-sector fluctuation pattern persists in hard--soft correlations. Predictions for D and B mesons extend the comparison to probes of different flavors. Taken together, these system-size, harmonic, fluctuation, and flavor dependences provide experimental tests of how far a common QGP description extends.

papers.title: Amplitudes separation and strong-electromagnetic phases determination in the $\boldsymbol{J/\psi}$ decays into baryon-antibaryon pairs
papers.abstract: We extract the relative phase between strong and electromagnetic amplitudes of the decays of a vector charmonium into spin-$1/2$ baryon-antibaryon pairs. Starting from a flavour-SU(3) effective Lagrangian with vector and tensor currents, we construct a parametrization in terms of partial waves coefficients. The electric and magnetic phases, the phase of the integrated complex overlap and the effective rate angle are derived from the same source amplitudes. We retain two possible solutions and both of them describe the scalar $\Sigma^+\bar\Sigma^-$ scan phase within its uncertainty, while presenting tension with several electric-magnetic production phases.

papers.title: Unpolarized proton PDF with physical quark masses and large momenta
papers.abstract: We present a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculation of the proton isovector ($u-d$) unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) at physical sea and valence quark masses, using Coulomb-gauge-fixed quark bilinears within the large-momentum effective theory framework. The calculation is performed on a (2+1)-flavor ensemble with a lattice spacing of $a=0.076$ fm and proton momenta up to $2.3$ GeV. We combine kinematically enhanced nucleon interpolating operators, the Coulomb-gauge method, and high-statistics measurements to improve the signal quality at large momenta and quark separations. We use the static regularization-independent momentum subtraction and hybrid schemes to renormalize the bare matrix elements. The light-cone PDF in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme is obtained from the quasi-PDF through next-to-leading-order (NLO) perturbative matching supplemented by next-to-leading-logarithmic renormalization-group resummation. With reduced uncertainties, the resulting PDF is consistent with our previous calculation on a similar lattice ensemble with $a=0.06$~fm and a valence pion mass of 300 MeV. Notably, despite the reduced uncertainties, the agreement with the phenomenological PDF persists over the longitudinal momentum fraction range $0.25\lesssim|x|\lesssim0.75$, where the lattice calculation is expected to be reliable. This agreement is further supported by a comparison in coordinate space, where our short-distance lattice matrix elements are consistent with those obtained from the phenomenological PDF through NLO matching. In particular, we observe close agreement in the imaginary part for the first time. Together, these results represent an encouraging step toward precision benchmarking of lattice QCD calculations of PDFs.

papers.title: Elliptic flow of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ via quark recombination mechanism in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: Multi-strange hadrons, such as the $\phi$ meson and $\Omega$ baryon, serve as unique probes for the properties of the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Using a quark recombination model with the quark phase-space information parameterized in a viscous blastwave, we show that the elliptic flow $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ can be describled by quark recombination in a wide energy range from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV. We check the scaling properties of $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ and find the number-of-constituent-quark (NCQ) scaled $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ are approximately equal. We further present the $v_2$ of strange quarks at hadronization extracted from $\phi$ and $\Omega$ data. We find the $v_2$ of strange quarks is close to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$ at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7-200 GeV, but significant larger than the latter at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76-5.02 TeV, suggesting that the $v_2$ of strange quarks cannot be simply equated to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $\phi$ and $\Omega$. Our results demonstrate that the quark recombination mechanism is valid for $\phi$ and $\Omega$ production in heavy-ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV, indicating the existence of constituent quark degree of freedom at these energies.

papers.title: Anomalous charge conjugation and parity in (2+1)-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly that involves $U(1)_Q$, $U(1)_F$, charge conjugation symmetry (acting only on $U(1)_Q$), and parity symmetry in $2+1$ dimensions. It is represented by a mutual Chern-Simons level $k_{QF}=\frac12 \,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z)$. Adopting the already established multi-charge anomaly sector, we explicitly provide the information that this response is $odd$ under $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ symmetries separately, but $even$ under combined $\mathsf{CP}$ symmetry. We also provide a global inflow representative and compute the equilibrium cross-charge response which includes $\partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4\pi \bmod 1/2\pi$. Using an analytic neutral-fluid example we show that this response is non-vanishing whereas the source-free hydrodynamic poles are invariant.

papers.title: Isospin violation and the neutron weak magnetic moment
papers.abstract: The recent measurement of weak magnetism in neutron beta decay [1] obtained a value that is consistent with the conserved vector current hypothesis requiring the assumption of isospin conservation. The influence of the quark-mass difference and electromagnetic effects that violate this conservation law are examined using non-relativistic constituent quark models and estimated to be of the order of at most 1%.

papers.title: Hall Viscosity in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
papers.abstract: We study the Hall viscosity of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) created in non-central heavy-ion collisions. In the presence of a strong magnetic field or vorticity, rotational symmetry is broken from $O(3)$ to $O(2)$, allowing for two independent Hall viscosities associated with shear deformations transverse and parallel to the symmetry-breaking direction. We find the corresponding constitutive relations by extending the kinetic-theory mechanism to three spatial dimensions and provide parametric estimates of the Hall viscosities under realistic QGP conditions. Both kinetic-theory and holographic estimates indicate that Hall viscosities are comparable in magnitude to the shear viscosity at zero magnetic field. We further show that Hall viscous stresses at hydrodynamic initialization can be as large as standard viscous corrections and identify observable consequences in flow and event-plane correlations.

papers.title: Dissipative properties of isoscalar collective excitations in heavy nuclei
papers.abstract: The dissipative properties of isoscalar collective motion in heavy nuclei are studied within a kinetic model of collective excitations in finite Fermi systems with a free moving surface. The model includes both the one-body damping produced by the interaction of nucleons with the dynamic surface of nucleus and the Landau damping mechanism. In this paper, we study the damping and dissipative properties of the isoscalar dipole collective modes and the isoscalar vortex octupole mode, which are formed due to dynamic effects of the nuclear surface. To study the damping mechanism of the considered collective modes, a multipole strength function is used in various approximations. It is shown that the damping of the considered isoscalar collective modes is due to a one-body damping mechanism. An analytical expression for the dissipation coefficient at finite frequency for the collective variable describing multipole oscillations of nuclear surface is obtained. It was found that the dissipation coefficient in the energy region of the considered isoscalar collective modes does not exceed the wall formula friction coefficient derived in the one-body dissipation theory. This result confirms the understanding of friction in the wall formula as a macroscopic limit of the one-body nuclear dissipation.

papers.title: Role of the scission-line structure in the formation of the fragment-mass distribution in $^{180}$Hg fission
papers.abstract: The fission of $^{180}\mathrm{Hg}$ is investigated by studying the stochastic evolution on the potential energy surface calculated within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree--Bogoliubov (MDC-RHB) model. The MDC-RHB model provides the zero-temperature potential-energy surface in the $(\beta_{20},\beta_{30})$ plane and self-consistent density distributions, from which scission configurations are identified using a geometrical neck criterion. The evolution toward scission is described by a master equation on the same deformation mesh, with transition rates determined by deformation-dependent microscopic level densities. The level densities are obtained in a finite-temperature BCS treatment using the MDC-RHB single-particle spectra and zero-temperature pairing gaps as input. The effective barrier-top region is found to lie close to the scission line, making the detailed energetic structure of the scission boundary particularly important for the fragment distribution. The potential-energy landscape and scission-line structure strongly favor reflection-asymmetric configurations with pronounced prefragment deformations and lead to fragment-mass distributions centered close to the experimentally observed $A_{\mathrm L}/A_{\mathrm H}\simeq80/100$ division. An additional constrained $\beta_{40}$ analysis indicates that fluctuations beyond the $(\beta_{20},\beta_{30})$ collective space can generate an additional spread of the fragment masses. With increasing excitation energy over the range $E^*=34.0$--$65.5$ MeV, the symmetric component is enhanced, while the asymmetric fission mode remains dominant.

papers.title: Spin Asymmetries for Twisted-Neutron Capture by Polarized $^3$He Nuclei
papers.abstract: We provide a theoretical analysis of a nuclear reaction caused by twisted neutrons that carry an additional Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) along the propagation direction. Angular momentum selection rules are derived for the thermal-neutron capture reaction on a spin-polarized $^3$He nucleus. We demonstrate that noticeable novel spin effects due to OAM are limited to the region of the size of de Broglie wavelength around the phase singularity of the beam. Spin asymmetries are predicted for a range of experimental constraints.

papers.title: Symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory
papers.abstract: A symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of the non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory is introduced. Integral equations for the two-nucleon scattering and the deuteron structure functions are derived and numerical solutions at leading order are obtained.

papers.title: Collective Signatures of Pionic Correlations at High Momentum Transfer
papers.abstract: High-momentum-transfer reactions have provided experimental evidence for enhanced pionic correlations in nuclei, yet the microscopic connection between the low-energy pionic response and the delta-hole excitation spectrum remains unresolved. Here we identify hybrid pion-delta collective modes that emerge through the coherent coupling of nucleon-hole and delta-hole excitations. By evaluating the full delta-hole Lindhard function within the random-phase approximation, we find a robust low-energy hybrid pion-delta mode and a higher-energy collective delta-hole mode. The low-energy mode is strongly enhanced as the Landau-Migdal parameter is reduced, exhibiting behavior characteristic of a precursor to pion condensation. We further show that these modes may be probed through high-momentum-transfer charged-pion production reactions. Because the same collective pion-delta function governs both the response and the RPA correlation energy, our results connect experimentally observable collective excitations with microscopic many-body correlations.

papers.title: Role of Wigner SU(4) Symmetry in Low-Energy Spin-Isospin Transitions of Three-Valence-Nucleon Systems on LS Closed Cores
papers.abstract: We investigate low-energy Fermi (F) and Gamow--Teller (GT) transition strengths in three-valence-nucleon systems from the viewpoint of Wigner SU(4) symmetry. For $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$, shell-model calculations show that the ground states contain a large component of the SU(4) representation whose spin-isospin wave function is fully antisymmetric. By varying the spin--orbit splitting in the shell-model Hamiltonian, we demonstrate clear correlations of the SU(4) overlap with both the GT strength to the ground state and its fraction of the total GT strength. For $^{7}{\rm Li}$--$^{7}{\rm Be}$, shell-model calculations show that the $3/2^-_\mathrm{g.s.}$ and $1/2^-_1$ states both belong predominantly to the same supermultiplet as the $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground states. The observed strong GT transitions to these states are therefore interpreted as transitions within the same SU(4) multiplet, split by the spin-orbit interaction. Thus, Wigner SU(4) symmetry provides a unified interpretation of low-energy GT strength concentrations in three-valence-nucleon systems. In particular, the concentration of both F and GT strengths in the same $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground-state transition is naturally understood as a three-valence-nucleon extension of the SU(4) mechanism underlying the low-energy strong GT peak in $^{18}{\rm O}$--$^{18}{\rm F}$.

papers.title: Proton Number Fluctuations in Au+Au and Ag+Ag Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$: A JAM Model Study
papers.abstract: Proton number fluctuations in low-energy heavy-ion collisions are sensitive to nuclear interactions, baryon-number conservation, and fluctuations of the collision volume, all of which can complicate searches for critical phenomena. We investigate proton-number cumulants and factorial cumulants up to fourth order in Au+Au and Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$ using the JAM hadronic transport model in cascade and mean-field modes. We employ the Centrality-Independent Genuine Cumulant Analysis fRamework (CIGAR) to suppress the initial-volume fluctuations and compare its results with those obtained using conventional centrality-bin-width corrections. CIGAR closely reproduces the participant-number-based reference, whereas the multiplicity-based analysis exhibits substantial deviations. In both collision systems, the ratios $C_{2}/C_{1}$, $C_{3}/C_{1}$, and $C_{4}/C_{2}$ generally decrease toward more central collisions and with increasing rapidity acceptance, while the mean field modifies their magnitudes. A simplified treatment of light-nucleus formation through probabilistic proton removal shifts $C_{4}/C_{2}$ toward less negative values. These results establish a hadronic-transport reference without an explicit QCD critical contribution and highlight the importance of controlling centrality fluctuations, acceptance, and light-nucleus formation when interpreting experimental measurements at high baryon density.

papers.title: Low-lying states of $^{115}$Cd modeled as a valence neutron coupled to $^{114}$Cd
papers.abstract: $^{114}$Cd has historically been regarded as an ideal quadrupole vibrator due to its near-canonical level spacings, though this interpretation is disputed due to electromagnetic transition data from the two- and three-phonon states. In this paper we investigate whether, with the extension of including the single-phonon octupole state, the model is still useful in describing the coupling of a neutron to a cadmium-114 core to model the lowest- energy cadmium-115 states, as the triplet states have small to no influence in the calculation. The results thus provide supporting evidence for the tentatively-assigned $J^\pi$ values of the lowest-energy $^{115}$Cd states. A more- rigorous derivation than often used for the vibrational B(E{\lambda}) is used, in conjunction with the $^{115}$Cd structure calculation, to provide a theoretical prediction of the $^{114}$Cd octupole deformation.

papers.title: On the Method of Projection onto Localized States for Describing Reactions and Clustering
papers.abstract: The method of projection onto localized states intended for describing reactions and clustering is examined. In particular, the method offers a simple extension of the no-core shell model to continuum- and clusterized bound states. A critical analysis of a previous realization of the method is provided. A way to minimize the number of basis functions required for convergence is given. An easy way to obtain exactly unitary and symmetric $S$ matrix from calculations is pointed out. The method is tested in one- and two-channel $np$ scattering problems with the Daejeon $NN$ interaction. It is shown that excellent convergence can be reached even when only oscillator states with low number of excitation quanta are retained.

papers.title: Emerging of massive gauge particles in inhomogeneous local gauge transformations
papers.abstract: A generalized theory of gauge transformations is presented on the basis of the covariant Hamiltonian formalism of field theory, for which the covariant canonical field equations are equivalent to the Euler-Lagrange field equations. Similar to the canonical transformation theory of point dynamics, the canonical transformation rules for fields are derived from generating functions. Thus---in contrast to the usual Lagrangian description---the covariant canonical transformation formalism automatically ensures the mappings to preserve the action principle, and hence to be {\em physical}. On that basis, we work out the theory of inhomogeneous local gauge transformations that generalizes the conventional local SU(N) gauge transformation theory. It is shown that massive gauge bosons naturally emerge in this description, which thus could supersede the Higgs mechanism.

papers.title: Neutron Star Mass-Radius Constraints for EXO 0748$-$676 from 2008-2025 Quiescent X-ray Spectra
papers.abstract: We present new constraints on the mass and radius of the neutron star in the neutron star low-mass X-ray binary EXO 0748$-$676 obtained from a joint analysis of 20 quiescent X-ray observations obtained between 2008 and 2025, including 14 Chandra and 6 XMM-Newton exposures. These data sample two quiescent episodes separated by the 2024$-$2025 outburst. We model the 0.5$-$10 keV spectra with a hydrogen-atmosphere model, assuming a source distance of 7.1 kpc. In a global Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis in which the hydrogen column density, neutron star mass, and radius are tied across all observations, we obtain a neutron-star mass of $1.77^{+0.17}_{-0.22}\,M_\odot$ and a radius of $12.62^{+0.56}_{-0.74}$ km ($1\sigma$ credible intervals). We further perform independent fits to the first and second quiescent epochs and find that the combined data set significantly reduces the low-mass tail in the posterior distribution, leading to tighter lower bounds on the neutron-star mass. Incorporating the distance uncertainty of $7.1\pm1.2$ kpc, we conservatively constrain the neutron-star mass and radius to $M\simeq 1.41-2.11~M_{\odot}$ and $R\simeq 10.15-15.13$ km, favoring relatively stiff dense-matter equations of state. We also trace the thermal evolution across two quiescent epochs and find evidence for renewed crust cooling following the 2024$-$2025 outburst, providing a unique opportunity to compare the thermal relaxation behavior after two distinct accretion episodes.

papers.title: Density-induced dark-baryon conversion in $\Delta-$admixed hypernuclear neutron stars
papers.abstract: We investigate density-induced conversion of neutrons into a neutral dark baryon $\chi$ in cold, charge-neutral, $\beta$-equilibrated neutron-star matter containing hyperons and all $\Delta(1232)$ quartet. The hadronic sector is modeled within a density-dependent covariant density-functional framework using the DDME2 parametrization. A scalar Higgs portal is included as a possible interaction channel between the visible and dark sectors, although its mean-field contribution is negligible for the couplings adopted here. Unlike fixed dark-matter admixture models or scenarios in which nucleon-to-DM conversion is driven by Higgs exchange, the $\chi$ abundance is determined self-consistently from chemical equilibrium and baryon-number conservation. We find that hyperons and $\Delta$ resonances alter the neutron chemical potential, delay the onset of $\chi$, and suppress its abundance relative to nucleonic matter. This competition induces characteristic changes in the equation of state, particle fractions, sound speed, and adiabatic index. For $m_\chi=1250$, $1300$, and $1400$ MeV, the maximum masses of the complete $N+Y+\Delta+\chi$ configurations are $1.806$, $1.899$ and $2.024,M_\odot$, respectively, indicating that the massive-pulsar constraint disfavors the lighter dark-baryon benchmarks. The radial profiles further show that for $m_\chi=1400$ MeV, $\chi$ is confined to the inner core of the most massive stars, while canonical configurations remain essentially unaffected. Thus, the stellar modifications arise primarily from conversion-induced rearrangement of the equilibrium composition rather than from Higgs-mediated interactions. These results highlight the importance of treating conventional non-nucleonic degrees of freedom and density-generated dark baryons on an equal footing when assessing the astrophysical viability of dark-sector extensions of dense matter.
